narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who end up departing.

Three factors stood out as the strongest drivers of this prediction. First, your overall career experience of 6–10 years pushed the prediction most strongly toward leaving. While many employees who stay have shorter experience (50% have only 1–5 years), the model sees mid-level experience like yours as a stage where people often begin exploring new opportunities.

Second, having received other job offers while working here was the next biggest influence, pulling the outcome further toward departure. This is relatively uncommon—only 23% of employees who stay report receiving outside offers—suggesting the model interprets these opportunities as a clear signal that you have viable alternatives.

Third, your 1–5 years with the current organization also contributed noticeably toward predicting you will leave. This shorter tenure in your present role, compared with longer-staying colleagues, reinforces the impression that you may still be evaluating whether this is your long-term fit.

Taken together, these elements created a profile the model associates with higher turnover risk. The organization should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether additional challenges, clearer growth paths, or retention measures could shift your trajectory. You, in turn, may want to reflect on what would make staying fulfilling before deciding on any external offers.
